summary_en: This Phase 2 trial tests a less frequent schedule of daratumumab with lenalidomide as maintenance therapy for multiple myeloma after a stem cell transplant. Daratumumab-hyaluronidase is given under the skin every 8 weeks in Year 1 and every 16 weeks in Years 2 through 4, and lenalidomide is taken by mouth once daily, starting at 10 mg and increasing to 15 mg if tolerated, until progression or unacceptable side effects. The main outcome is not stated; the study is a Phase 2 trial.
summary_es: Este ensayo de fase 2 evalúa un esquema de daratumumab con menor frecuencia junto con lenalidomida como terapia de mantenimiento para el mieloma múltiple después de un trasplante de células madre. El daratumumab con hialuronidasa se aplica debajo de la piel cada 8 semanas durante el primer año y cada 16 semanas en los años 2 a 4, y la lenalidomida se toma por vía oral una vez al día, comenzando con 10 mg y aumentando a 15 mg si se tolera, hasta la progresión de la enfermedad o efectos secundarios inaceptables. El resultado principal no se indica en el registro; el estudio es un ensayo de fase 2.
who_for: Newly diagnosed multiple myeloma, age 18 to 70, after stem cell transplant with partial response or better.
Induction treatment included a proteasome inhibitor, an immunomodulatory drug, and an anti-CD38 antibody.
Blood counts, liver and kidney function within the study's stated limits.
Those who could become pregnant must use birth control and have pregnancy testing.
not_for: Concomitant amyloidosis or plasma cell leukemia.
Pregnant or breastfeeding, or a live vaccine within 30 days before the first dose.
Participation in another investigational study within 4 weeks before the first dose.
Immunodeficiency, or steroid use above 10 mg daily prednisone equivalent.
Another cancer progressing or treated within 3 years, brain or meningeal spread, or recent severe heart disease or stroke.
